name: E2E Networks
tagline: NSE-listed Indian GPU cloud and CPU infrastructure for AI workloads
description: E2E Networks is an NSE-listed Indian cloud provider offering NVIDIA GPU cloud, CPU compute instances and cloud infrastructure built for AI and developer workloads, not shared hosting.
about: E2E Networks is India's only publicly listed pure-play GPU cloud company, trading on the NSE and BSE. It runs data centers in Delhi NCR, Mumbai and Bengaluru and focuses on NVIDIA GPU cloud (B200, H200, H100 and L4 instances) alongside standard CPU compute nodes, aimed squarely at AI training/inference workloads, developers and startups rather than at website owners.

Billing is transparent pay-as-you-go with per-minute granularity on GPU nodes: published rates include NVIDIA H100 around $2.69/hour, H200 around $3.99/hour and B200 around $6.99/hour, alongside cheaper L4 instances near $0.57/hour. CPU-only compute starts much lower — E2E's entry-level C3 and E1 series instances run roughly $0.044-$0.096/hour (about $32-$70/month). Monthly and longer-term commitments bring further discounts of roughly 10-30% off the hourly rate. E2E updated its published GPU, compute and storage pricing effective July 1, 2026, so check the live pricing page for current rates before committing.

There is no cPanel, no shared-hosting-style website builder and no email hosting bundled in — provisioning is instance-based (Linux/Windows VM images, containers, and managed Kubernetes for GPU workloads), so this is infrastructure for teams running their own applications or ML pipelines, not a plug-and-play website host.
policies: E2E Networks does not publish a blanket money-back guarantee comparable to consumer web hosts; billing is usage-based (pay-as-you-go or committed term), so review the specific refund/cancellation terms on your invoice or contract before committing to a longer prepaid term.

E2E Networks has very little public review presence — its Trustpilot profile is unclaimed with only 7 reviews and a 2.3/5 average, so treat that rating as a small, mixed sample rather than a definitive verdict.
